Protect corridors and sites

Excavations, pits and ground disturbance, mapped between dates

Third-party works near a pipeline or cable, and surface excavations on a mining right, usually show at the surface before anyone reports them. We map fresh digging, pits, spoil heaps, trenches, water-filled excavations and new tracks between dated surveys, and flag each one so your field teams know where to check. We describe the ground, never the people.

Used in: Oil & gas · Mining · Telecom fibre · Rail & roads

Request a proposal How change is checked

What it is

The digging that comes before the problem

On a pipeline or cable right of way, third-party works are one of the main threats to the line: a trench for a water pipe, a borrow pit for a road, foundations for a new building, earthworks for a farm dam. They are visible from above as fresh digging, spoil heaps and new tracks, often before anyone reports them.

On a mining right, surface excavation by others changes the ground you are answerable for: pits, disturbed ground, spoil and water-filled excavations inside the concession or around its edge, often growing between visits.

We map those features between dated surveys, flag each new or growing site with its location, size on the imagery and distance to your line or boundary, and a reviewer confirms each one before it reaches you. The result is a list of places for your field teams to check. It tells them where to look; it does not replace them.

Land, never people

We describe excavations, pits, spoil, water-filled pits and tracks. We never count, describe or identify the people involved, and we never attribute ground disturbance to anyone. Whether works are authorised is for you and the authorities to decide.

How it works

Two jobs, one method

Pipelines and cables

Works on rights of way

Fresh digging, spoil heaps, trenches and earthworks on or near your pipeline or cable right of way, flagged between surveys and listed by chainage and distance to the line, so your field teams know where to check first.

Concessions and reserves

Surface excavation on mining rights

Pits, disturbed ground, spoil heaps and water-filled excavations mapped inside and around your mining right or concession, with new sites flagged between dates and listed by zone.

  1. Imagery to match the features

    Very-high-resolution satellite scenes or drone orthophotos for individual excavations; open satellite data and global disturbance alerts for larger disturbed areas across a wide concession. Radar comparisons show larger earthworks even under rainy-season cloud.

  2. Detection tuned to your ground

    Detection of excavations, spoil and pits is tuned to your imagery and checked on part of your area before it runs on the rest.

  3. Flag and confirm

    New and growing features are flagged between dated surveys and confirmed by a reviewer, with before-and-after views. New tracks and access roads are mapped alongside.

  4. Tell your field teams

    A notice after each survey lists the sites to check, by chainage or zone, with coordinates your teams can navigate to.

What you receive

A list of places to check

  • A flagged-site list: each excavation, pit, spoil heap or trench with ID, coordinates, chainage or zone, distance to your line or boundary, and the dates between which it appeared or grew
  • Before-and-after views of each flagged site
  • New tracks and access roads into the area, mapped between dates
  • Disturbance notices from global alert systems for wide concessions, checked by our team
  • A PDF report in English or Portuguese, GIS layers in GeoPackage, GeoJSON, KMZ and Shapefile, and an interactive map file for field teams

The services behind it

Every proposal names the services it includes. These are the ones this solution draws on.

Change and repeat surveys

  • Forest-loss and ground-disturbance alertsRegular notices of tree-cover loss and ground disturbance inside or near your estate or concession, drawn from global satellite alert systems and checked by our team.
  • All-weather radar change screeningRadar satellite comparisons that show larger ground changes, such as clearing, earthworks and new large buildings, even under rainy-season cloud.

Detection of specific features

  • Track and access-route mappingNew tracks and access roads into your concession, across your right of way or around your site, mapped between dates.
  • Artisanal mining and excavation mappingPits, disturbed ground, spoil heaps and water-filled excavations mapped inside and around your mining right or concession, with new sites flagged between dates.
  • Excavation and third-party works on rights of wayFresh digging, spoil heaps, trenches and earthworks on or near your pipeline or cable right of way, flagged between surveys so your field teams know where to check.

Limits

What excavation mapping is not

What it shows

  • Excavations, spoil, pits and tracks visible at the surface on dated imagery
  • Where they appeared or grew between surveys
  • Their distance to your line or boundary

What it does not show

  • Leaks, taps, theft, corrosion or the condition of any pipe or cable
  • Underground workings, or shafts under cover
  • Features under tree canopy, which can be missed
  • Anything about the people involved

Who uses it

Owners of lines and land where digging matters

Oil & gas

Right-of-way and damage-prevention teams on gas, crude and fuel pipelines, who need to know where third-party works have started near the line.

Pipeline rights of way

Mining

Surface excavation

Telecom fibre

Wayleave, patrol and planned-works teams on buried fibre routes, who need to know where fresh digging has started near the route.

Route patrols and planned works

Also used by power utilities along buried cables, by road and rail agencies on their reserves and beside freight lines, and by estates and conservation areas.

Frequently asked questions

Can this detect leaks, taps or theft from a pipeline?

No. We flag works visible at the surface, such as fresh digging, spoil heaps and trenches near the line, so your field teams know where to check. We make no claim about what is happening underground or to the pipe, and it never replaces your patrols or integrity programme.

Do you identify who is digging?

No. We map excavations, pits, spoil and tracks, never people, and we never attribute ground disturbance to anyone. Results go only to the contacts you name, and what you share with authorities is your decision.

Can you see underground workings or shafts?

No. Only what is visible from above is mapped. Underground workings and shafts under cover cannot be seen on satellite or drone imagery.

How small an excavation can you see?

It depends on the imagery. Very-high-resolution satellite scenes and drone orthophotos show much smaller features than open satellite data, which picks up larger disturbed areas. We agree the imagery with you to match the size of the features that matter, and tune detection on part of your area before it runs on the rest.

Tell us where digging near your assets worries you.

A right of way, a mining right or a site boundary, and the widths to watch. We reply with an imagery plan and a written proposal.
